title: Site check: can Muse Spark reading the aerial photo, confirmed by SAM 3.1, tell what a corner already has?
registered: validation/BENCH_PREREG.md, T16 (2026-11-01, before any new aerial photo was fetched for it or any model looked at one)
corners: all screened corners with an aerial photo
image: the state orthophoto (NYS GIS Program Office) through brief.aerial: 768 x 768 px over 180 m, centred on the corner

high_visibility_crosswalk.truth: OpenStreetMap crossing nodes within 40 m: crossing:markings zebra or ladder (any variant) = yes; lines, dashes, surface or no = no; untagged = unknown (excluded)

bike_lane.truth: NYC Bike Routes (mzxg-pwib) within 40 m with facility class I or II = yes, otherwise no (class III shared lanes are not painted lanes)

median.truth: NYC Planimetric Median (ees7-4ufv) polygon within 40 m = yes, otherwise no

arms.spark: Muse Spark (Meta API) answers present / absent / unsure per attribute with points on the image
arms.sam: SAM 3.1 image segmentation of the concept: present when its detections cover at least 0.2% of the 40 m circle
arms.gated: present only when Spark says present and a SAM 3.1 detection lies within 15 m of one of Spark's points; absent when Spark says absent and SAM finds nothing in the circle; otherwise unsure

metrics: accuracy on decided corners per attribute and arm, with Wilson 95% interval
for the gated arm: how many top-fix recommendations change (Crosswalk Visibility Enhancements marked as already present)
rule: An attribute's gated answer is used in the product only if its gated accuracy is at least 0.85 with coverage at least 0.5; otherwise it is shown but does not change any recommendation. Everything is reported either way.
